question.text: Two particles begin their motion at the same instant along the x-axis. Particle 1 is initially located at x = − 10 m, moving with a speed of 4 m/s in the negative x-direction while experiencing an acceleration of 2 m/s² in the positive x-direction. Particle 2 is initially positioned at x = + 2 m, possessing an initial speed of 6 m/s in the positive x-direction and an acceleration of 2 m/s² in the negative x-direction. Determine:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: The time elapsed until the particles collide.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: The position coordinate (x) at which the collision occurs.

conditions: Particle 1: initial position x = − 10 m, initial velocity = − 4 m/s, acceleration = + 2 m/s²
Particle 2: initial position x = + 2 m, initial velocity = + 6 m/s, acceleration = − 2 m/s²

figure.description: A horizontal x-axis displaying two particles. Particle 1 is at coordinate x = − 10 m with an initial velocity vector pointing leftward of magnitude 4 m/s and an acceleration vector pointing rightward of magnitude 2 m/s². Particle 2 is at coordinate x = + 2 m with an initial velocity vector pointing rightward of magnitude 6 m/s and an acceleration vector pointing leftward of magnitude 2 m/s².

solution.approach: Write the position of each particle as a function of time and solve for the time at which the two positions are equal.

steps.text: Write the position of particle 1, starting at x = −10 m with velocity −4 m/s and acceleration +2 m/s².
Write the position of particle 2, starting at x = +2 m with velocity +6 m/s and acceleration −2 m/s².
Set the two positions equal and solve the resulting quadratic for t, keeping the positive root.
Substitute t = 6 s into either position equation to get the collision point.

common_mistakes.text: Taking t = −1 s, the other root of the quadratic, as the collision time, which is not physical since time cannot be negative.
Writing particle 1's acceleration term as −t² instead of +t² by keeping the sign of its velocity for the acceleration too, which changes the quadratic and its root.
